methodology: challenge-assumptions

# Food-safety audit findings

The annual food-safety audit for the specialty-food segment came back clean this year, but the auditor's informal comments afterward were more interesting than the formal report: she mentioned, unprompted, that a cosmetics or skincare client asking about cold-chain transport would fall under a noticeably lighter regulatory regime than either pharmaceuticals or food, since most personal-care products in this category are not classified as requiring the same chain-of-custody documentation.

Nobody on the team had actually assumed that; the working assumption going into the audit conversation was that any new segment beyond food and pharma would probably need a comparable compliance build, similar in weight to the pharmacy process. If the auditor's informal read holds up under a proper check, it would mean the smallest regulatory lift of any plausible new segment is not the dairy business the team already knows, but a category nobody in this room had seriously considered, worth confirming with someone whose job is actually regulatory rather than food-safety specifically.
